def-csm-frontier-ssep-weak-heat-solution:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), meaning every at most countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $d\ge1$, let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ carry the normalized product Haar measure $dx$ with $dx(\mathbb T^d)=1$, and let $\rho_0$ be a real measurable function on $\mathbb T^d$ with $0\le\rho_0\le1$ almost everywhere. For a finite $T\ge0$, a **weak heat solution with datum $\rho_0$** is a family $(u_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ of real essentially bounded measurable-function classes (elements of $L^\infty(\mathbb T^d,dx;\mathbb R)$), with $u_0=\rho_0$ as a function class, such that for every complex-valued smooth periodic test function $G$, the map $t\mapsto\int_{\mathbb T^d}u_t(x)G(x)\,dx$ is continuous and

$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}u_t(x)G(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_0(x)G(x)\,dx+\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb T^d}u_s(x)\Delta G(x)\,dx\,ds$$

for every $0\le t\le T$. Here $\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^d\partial_{x_i}^2$ is the periodic Laplacian; equality of function classes means equality almost everywhere with respect to $dx$. For the Fourier convention on this torus, set $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ for $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ and $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$ for $f\in L^1(\mathbb T^d,dx)$.
lem-csm-frontier-ssep-sector-connectivit:
## Statement

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected simple undirected graph with $m:=|V|\ge1$. For $0\le k\le m$, let $\mathcal C_k(G)$ be the set of all $k$-element subsets of $V$. Join distinct $A,B\in\mathcal C_k(G)$ when there is an edge $\{x,y\}\in E$ with $x\in A$, $y\notin A$, and $B=(A\setminus\{x\})\cup\{y\}$. Then this graph on $\mathcal C_k(G)$ is connected.
lem-csm-frontier-ssep-heat-flow:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$ and let $\rho_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $0\le\rho_0\le1$ almost everywhere, using normalized product Haar measure $dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ define $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ and $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$. For $t>0$ set

$$\rho_t(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat\rho_0(k)e_k(x),$$

and at $t=0$ set $\rho_t=\rho_0$ as an almost-everywhere class. For smooth periodic $G$, define

$$P_tG(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat G(k)e_k(x)\quad(t>0),\qquad P_0G:=G.$$

Then on every strip $[\epsilon,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ with $0<\epsilon<T<\infty$, the series for $\rho_t$ and all its space and time derivatives converge absolutely and uniformly; in particular $\rho_t$ is real and smooth for each $t>0$ and $\partial_t\rho_t=\Delta\rho_t$. For every finite $T$ and every smooth $G$, $P_tG$ is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$, satisfies $\partial_tP_tG=\Delta P_tG$, has uniformly bounded derivatives of every fixed order there, and $P_tG\to G$ uniformly as $t\downarrow0$. Moreover

$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_tG\,dx=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_0P_tG\,dx,$$

so $(\rho_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ is the unique weak heat solution with datum $\rho_0$ in the stated weak formulation. It preserves $0\le\rho_t\le1$ almost everywhere and the mass $\int\rho_t\,dx=\int\rho_0\,dx$.
def-csm-frontier-ssep-diffusive-model:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice, meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and an integer $N\ge3$. Let $\Lambda_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$, with each coordinate represented by $0,1,\ldots,N-1$, and let $\mathcal E_N$ be the set of unordered nearest-neighbor bonds $\{x,x+e_i\}$, where $1\le i\le d$ and addition is modulo $N$. The condition $N\ge3$ makes this a simple graph with each bond listed once as $x$ ranges over $\Lambda_N$. The site graph is connected because any two coordinate tuples are joined by finitely many steps of $+e_i$ or $-e_i$.

The configuration space is $\Omega_N=\{\eta:\Lambda_N\to\{0,1\}\}$, ordered lexicographically by its binary occupation vector in the fixed site order; this labels it as a finite set $\{1,\ldots,2^{N^d}\}$. The occupation $\eta_x$ is $1$ for an occupied site and $0$ for a vacant site. For $b=\{x,y\}\in\mathcal E_N$, let $\eta^b$ be the configuration obtained by swapping $\eta_x$ and $\eta_y$.

The coordinates $x/N$ have dimensionless spacing $1/N$ on the unit torus, and $t$ is dimensionless diffusive time: it is the microscopic unit-rate bond clock accelerated by the factor $N^2$. Thus the continuum heat equation below has normalized diffusion coefficient $D=1$.

Define a rate matrix $L_N$ on $\Omega_N$ by giving each distinct state change $\eta\to\eta^b\ne\eta$ rate $N^2$ and setting the diagonal entry to the negative sum of the off-diagonal row. If the two occupations on a bond agree, swapping them produces no state change and contributes no off-diagonal transition. On a column observable $f:\Omega_N\to\mathbb R$, use the row-generator convention $(L_Nf)(\eta)=\sum_{\xi\ne\eta}L_N(\eta,\xi)(f(\xi)-f(\eta))$; a row probability vector evolves by $p'=pL_N$. The **symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP)** is the uniformized finite-state chain with rate matrix $L_N$ and any specified initial probability vector. The finite-generator existence result supplies its all-pairs transition matrices $e^{tL_N}$ and càdlàg paths. Every jump conserves $\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\eta_x$.

For $k=0,1,\ldots,N^d$, the fixed-occupancy sector is $\Omega_{N,k}=\{\eta\in\Omega_N:\sum_x\eta_x=k\}$. When $0<k<N^d$, this sector has at least two states and its transition graph is connected by the fixed-occupancy connectivity lemma. Setting every sector energy to $0$, $\beta=1$, and each allowed transition rate to $N^2$ makes this sector a finite reversible stochastic rate model with uniform stationary weights. The sectors $k=0$ and $k=N^d$ are singleton constant chains. The full SSEP state graph is reducible across particle-number sectors; the generic finite rate-matrix construction, not the irreducible reversible-model definition, defines the full process.

Let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized Haar measure $dx$. For $x\in\Lambda_N$, write $x/N\in\mathbb T^d$ for the point with coordinates represented in $[0,1)$. The empirical measure and its action on a smooth periodic test function $G$ are

$$\pi_t^N:=N^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\eta_x(t)\,\delta_{x/N},\qquad \langle\pi_t^N,G\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb T^d}G\,d\pi_t^N=N^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\eta_x(t)G(x/N).$$

Here $\delta_y$ denotes unit point mass at $y$. Thus $\pi_t^N$ is a finite positive measure of total mass at most $1$, not necessarily a probability measure. For a smooth periodic $G$, define its discrete Laplacian on grid points by

$$\Delta_NG(x/N):=N^2\sum_{i=1}^d\bigl[G((x+e_i)/N)+G((x-e_i)/N)-2G(x/N)\bigr].$$
lem-csm-frontier-ssep-bracket:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $N\ge3$, $T\ge0$, and let $(\eta_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be the SSEP from the diffusive-model definition with any initial probability vector. For a real smooth periodic $G:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$, set

$$M_t^{N,G}:=\langle\pi_t^N,G\rangle-\langle\pi_0^N,G\rangle-\int_0^t\langle\pi_s^N,\Delta_NG\rangle\,ds.$$

Then $M^{N,G}$ is a square-integrable martingale. Its continuous predictable bracket is

$$A_t^{N,G}=N^{2-2d}\int_0^t\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}(\eta_{x+e_i}(s)-\eta_x(s))^2\bigl(G((x+e_i)/N)-G(x/N)\bigr)^2\,ds,$$

in the continuous predictable compensator convention of the finite-chain martingale supplier. In particular,

$$A_T^{N,G}\le T N^{-d}\sum_{i=1}^d\|\partial_iG\|_\infty^2.$$
lem-csm-frontier-ssep-time-dependent-mar:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $N\ge3$, $T\ge0$, and let $(\eta_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be the SSEP from the diffusive-model definition. Let $H:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be smooth up to the time endpoints, meaning all time and space derivatives used below extend continuously to $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$. Define

$$F_s^N(\eta):=N^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\eta_xH(s,x/N),\qquad 0\le s\le T.$$

Then

$$M_t^N:=F_t^N(\eta_t)-F_0^N(\eta_0)-\int_0^t\langle\pi_s^N,\partial_sH(s,\cdot)+\Delta_NH(s,\cdot)\rangle\,ds$$

is a square-integrable martingale, and

$$A_t^N:=N^{2-2d}\int_0^t\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}(\eta_{x+e_i}(s)-\eta_x(s))^2\bigl(H(s,(x+e_i)/N)-H(s,x/N)\bigr)^2\,ds$$

is a continuous predictable increasing process with $(M_t^N)^2-A_t^N$ a martingale. In particular,

$$A_T^N\le T N^{-d}\sum_{i=1}^d\sup_{0\le s\le T}\|\partial_iH(s,\cdot)\|_\infty^2.$$
thm-csm-frontier-ssep-heat-limit:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $d\ge1$, $T\ge0$, and for each integer $N\ge3$ let $(\eta_t^N)_{0\le t\le T}$ be the SSEP on $\Lambda_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ with rate $N^2$ on each unordered nearest-neighbor bond, started from any initial probability vector on a probability space $(\Xi_N,\mathcal A_N,\mathbb P_N)$. Write $\pi_t^N=N^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\eta_x^N(t)\delta_{x/N}$ for its empirical measure. Suppose a measurable $\rho_0:\mathbb T^d\to[0,1]$ satisfies, for every real-valued smooth periodic $G$ and every $\epsilon>0$,

$$\mathbb P_N\!\left(\left|\langle\pi_0^N,G\rangle-\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_0(x)G(x)\,dx\right|>\epsilon\right)\longrightarrow0\qquad(N\to\infty),$$

where the probability spaces may depend on $N$. Let $\rho_t$ be the unique weak heat solution on $\mathbb T^d$ with initial datum $\rho_0$, defined by the Fourier heat profile. Then for every real-valued smooth periodic $G$ and every $\epsilon>0$,

$$\mathbb P_N\!\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left|\langle\pi_t^N,G\rangle-\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_t(x)G(x)\,dx\right|>\epsilon\right)\longrightarrow0\qquad(N\to\infty).$$
